accepted.s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Gupta dynasty and bore the title ‘Maharaja’?
accepted.x: Sri Gupta, who ruled approximately from 240 to 280 CE, is regarded as the founder of the Gupta dynasty and bore the title ‘Maharaja’.
accepted.tq: Use direct founder–title recall.
accepted.sec: Chronological order of Gupta rulers (Chandragupta I to Vishnugupta)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ghatotkacha ruled approximately during which period?
accepted.x: Ghatotkacha ruled approximately from 280 to 319 CE, succeeding Sri Gupta.
accepted.tq: Distinguish adjacent Gupta reign periods through numerical recall.
accepted.sec: Chronological order of Gupta rulers (Chandragupta I to Vishnugupta)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Gupta Era is generally associated with the accession of which ruler and the year 319–320 CE?
accepted.x: Chandragupta I ruled approximately from 319 to 335 CE, and the Gupta Era is associated with 319–320 CE.
accepted.tq: Link a historical era with its ruler and date.
accepted.sec: Chronological order of Gupta rulers (Chandragupta I to Vishnugupta)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Chandragupta I ruled approximately from 319 to 335 CE. The period c. 335–375 CE belongs to Samudragupta.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed adjacent reign period.
accepted.sec: Chronological order of Gupta rulers (Chandragupta I to Vishnugupta)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the later Gupta rulers:
1. Vishnugupta was the last ruler of the main Gupta line.
2. Vishnugupta ruled approximately from 540 to 550 CE.
3. Purugupta, Kumaragupta II, Budhagupta, Narasimhagupta and Kumaragupta III belonged to the later Gupta succession.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Vishnugupta was the last ruler of the main line and ruled approximately from 540 to 550 CE; the other named rulers belonged to the later Gupta succession.
accepted.tq: Check the ruler list, terminal ruler and date together.
accepted.sec: Chronological order of Gupta rulers (Chandragupta I to Vishnugupta)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was borne by Chandragupta II?
accepted.x: Chandragupta II bore the title Vikramaditya. He was also known by the title Simhavikrama.
accepted.tq: Use direct ruler–title identification.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Chandragupta II was also known by which of the following names?
1. Devagupta
2. Devaraja
3. Baladitya
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Chandragupta II was also known as Devagupta and Devaraja. Baladitya was associated with Narasimhagupta, not Chandragupta II.
accepted.tq: Separate alternative names from names of other Gupta rulers.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The title ‘Simhavikrama’ of Chandragupta II is particularly associated with which type of coin?
accepted.x: Chandragupta II issued lion-slayer coins and used the title Simhavikrama. His father is associated with tiger-slayer coins.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the lion-slayer and tiger-slayer coin types.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which ruler was defeated by Chandragupta II in the Saka conquest?
accepted.x: Chandragupta II defeated Rudrasimha III and annexed western Malwa and Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–conquest association.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following regions were annexed by Chandragupta II after his Saka conquest?
accepted.x: Chandragupta II annexed western Malwa and Gujarat after defeating Rudrasimha III.
accepted.tq: Match the conquest with its territorial result.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Udayagiri cave inscription recording the Saka campaign of Chandragupta II is associated with which person?
accepted.x: The Udayagiri cave inscription of Virasena records the campaign of Chandragupta II against the Sakas.
accepted.tq: Use inscription–author association rather than ruler recall alone.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which inscription claims the extension of Chandragupta II’s authority towards north-western India and Bengal?
accepted.x: The Mehrauli iron pillar inscription claims Chandragupta II’s achievements in north-western India and Bengal.
accepted.tq: Distinguish inscriptions by the geographical claim they make.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Why are the silver coins of Chandragupta II regarded as strong evidence of his victory over the Sakas?
o: They were issued exclusively in western Malwa before the conquest.
They imitated Saka silver coins and were issued after the conquest.
They carried the portrait of Rudrasimha III.
They were the first Gupta coins issued in gold.
accepted.x: The silver coins of Chandragupta II were modelled on Saka silver coins and were issued after the Saka conquest, making them strong evidence of that victory.
accepted.tq: Infer historical evidence from the design, timing and material of coins.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Saka-model silver coins of Chandragupta II weighed approximately:
accepted.x: The Saka-model silver coins of Chandragupta II weighed approximately 33 grains.
accepted.tq: Test the precise quantitative detail with close numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Alliance)
A. Naga
B. Vakataka
C. Dhruvadevi

List-II (Detail)
1. Prabhavati married Rudrasena II
2. Marriage after the killing of Ramagupta
3. Marriage with Kuberanaga

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Chandragupta II married Kuberanaga, a Naga princess; his daughter Prabhavati married Vakataka ruler Rudrasena II; Dhruvadevi was married after Ramagupta’s killing.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure alliance–marriage pair and eliminate the codes.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the political significance of Prabhavati Gupta’s marriage to Rudrasena II?
o: It led to the direct annexation of Magadha by the Vakatakas.
It established Ujjain as the Vakataka capital.
It enabled indirect Gupta control over the Vakataka kingdom.
It ended Gupta control over western Malwa.
accepted.x: Prabhavati Gupta’s marriage to Vakataka ruler Rudrasena II enabled Chandragupta II to exercise indirect control over the Vakataka kingdom.
accepted.tq: Identify the political consequence of a matrimonial alliance.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Fa-Hien visited India approximately during which period?
accepted.x: Fa-Hien visited India approximately from 399 to 414 CE, during the reign of Chandragupta II.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the pilgrim’s travel period from neighbouring Gupta reigns.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Fa-Hien’s account is correct?
o: He explicitly named Chandragupta II as the reigning king in every account.
He visited India during the reign of Skandagupta to study military administration.
He did not name the king because his principal concern was Buddhism.
He was a Gupta court official appointed at Ujjain.
accepted.x: Fa-Hien was a Buddhist pilgrim, and he did not name the reigning king because his focus was Buddhism rather than political history.
accepted.tq: Reject the tempting but unsupported courtier and ruler-identification claims.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the traditional Navaratnas of Chandragupta II?
accepted.x: Fa-Hien was a visiting Buddhist pilgrim, not one of the traditional Navaratnas. Kalidasa, Amarasimha and Varahamihira are included in the traditional list.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a well-known named list.
accepted.sec: Chandragupta II - titles and other names, Saka conquest evidence, silver coins, matrimonial alliances, Fa-Hien's visit, Navaratnas  [APPSC]

Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the traditional Navaratnas of Chandragupta II?
1. Kalidasa — Navaratna
2. Dhanvantari — Navaratna
3. Kshapanaka — Navaratna
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Kalidasa, Dhanvantari and Kshapanaka are all included in the traditional list of nine gems. The full list also includes Amarasimha, Varahamihira, Vararuchi, Shanku, Ghatakarpara and Vetalabhatta.
accepted.tq: Verify multiple members of a named traditional list.

accepted.s: The first Huna attack on the Gupta Empire occurred during the reign of:
accepted.x: The first Huna attack occurred during the reign of Kumaragupta I. It was repulsed by Prince Skandagupta.
accepted.tq: Separate the Gupta ruler during the first attack from the ruler who repelled it.

accepted.x: Prince Skandagupta repelled the first Huna attack, which took place during the reign of Kumaragupta I.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the attacked ruler and the military defender.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Hunas who entered India in the mid-fifth century were also known as:
accepted.x: The Hunas were Hephthalites, also called White Huns. They came from Central Asia through the Oxus valley.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely associated Central Asian peoples by their alternative names.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The initial route and early area of Huna expansion in India were respectively:
accepted.x: The Hephthalite or White Huns entered from Central Asia through the Oxus valley and occupied Gandhara.
accepted.tq: Match the invasion route with the first occupied region.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Skandagupta’s Huna campaigns:
1. He repulsed the Hunas twice.
2. He assumed the title Vikramaditya after his victories.
3. His campaigns belonged to the reign of Kumaragupta I alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Skandagupta repulsed the Hunas twice and took the title Vikramaditya. The later Huna waves occurred during his own reign, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Detect the statement that improperly confines a continuing invasion to one reign.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the Huna leaders and the Indian rulers associated with their defeat?
o: Toramana—no defeat stated; Mihirakula—Yashodharman and Narasimhagupta Baladitya
accepted.x: Toramana occupied large parts of western and central India, while Mihirakula was defeated by Yashodharman, Narasimhagupta Baladitya and the Maukharis.
accepted.tq: Separate the territorial advance of Toramana from the recorded defeat of Mihirakula.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
By approximately 485 CE, which of the following areas were held by the Hunas?
1. Punjab
2. Rajasthan
3. Kashmir
4. Eastern Malwa and central India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: By 485 CE, the Hunas held Punjab, Rajasthan, Kashmir, eastern Malwa and central India.
accepted.tq: Test the complete territorial extent rather than one isolated region.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement about Mihirakula is correct?
o: He was defeated by Rudrasimha III in western Malwa.
He was the father of Toramana and patronised Buddhism.
He led the first Huna attack during Kumaragupta I’s reign.
He was the son of Toramana and persecuted Buddhists.
accepted.x: Mihirakula was the son of Toramana. He was described as a tyrant and iconoclast who persecuted Buddhists.
accepted.tq: Use the father–son relationship and religious policy as distinguishing clues.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. First Huna attack
B. Later Huna waves
C. Toramana
D. Mihirakula

List-II
1. Narasimhagupta’s reign
2. Late Kumaragupta I’s reign
3. Skandagupta’s reign
4. Budhagupta and after

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The first attack occurred during late Kumaragupta I; later waves during Skandagupta; Toramana advanced under Budhagupta and after; Mihirakula is associated with Narasimhagupta’s reign.
accepted.tq: Start with the fixed first-attack and later-wave pairs.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Skandagupta faced which two major threats during his reign?
accepted.x: Skandagupta faced the Pushyamitras, particularly at the end of Kumaragupta’s reign, and the Hunas during his own reign.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact pair of invasions faced by a ruler.

accepted.s: The Bhitari pillar inscription of Skandagupta is located in present-day:
accepted.x: The Bhitari pillar is located at Ghazipur in Uttar Pradesh and records Skandagupta’s victories over the Pushyamitras and Hunas.
accepted.tq: Match an inscription with its location and content.
accepted.sec: Skandagupta - invasions faced, inscriptions (Bhitari, Junagadh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which inscription records the repair of the Sudarshana lake by Parnadatta, the governor of Skandagupta?
accepted.x: The Junagadh, or Girnar, inscription records that Parnadatta repaired the Sudarshana lake while serving as Skandagupta’s governor.
accepted.tq: Use the public-works detail to identify the correct inscription.
accepted.sec: Skandagupta - invasions faced, inscriptions (Bhitari, Junagadh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following features is depicted on Skandagupta’s gold coins?
o: A ship, a wheel and a seated Buddha
A tiger, a horse and a sacrificial altar
A bow and arrow, the Garuda standard and Lakshmi
A lion, a trident and Nandi
accepted.x: Skandagupta’s gold coins depict him with a bow and arrow, the Garuda standard and Lakshmi.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive iconography of a ruler’s coinage.
accepted.sec: Skandagupta - invasions faced, inscriptions (Bhitari, Junagadh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which institutional change is associated with Skandagupta’s reign?
o: Governors became hereditary feudatories as central control weakened.
The Gupta Empire became a federation of independent republics immediately.
Provincial offices were transferred exclusively to Buddhist monasteries.
Governors were abolished and all provinces were directly administered from Pataliputra.
accepted.x: Central control weakened under Skandagupta, and governors increasingly became hereditary feudatories.
accepted.tq: Infer administrative decentralisation from the change in provincial offices.
accepted.sec: Skandagupta - invasions faced, inscriptions (Bhitari, Junagadh)  [other exams]

accepted.s: The account of the Ramagupta episode is found in which work by Vishakhadatta?
accepted.x: The Ramagupta episode is narrated in Devichandraguptam, attributed to Vishakhadatta.
accepted.tq: Match the historical episode with its literary source.
accepted.sec: Ramagupta episode - source text, succession dispute  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ramagupta episode:
1. Ramagupta was the elder brother of Chandragupta II.
2. Ramagupta agreed to surrender Dhruvadevi to a Saka king.
3. Chandragupta II killed the Saka king, subsequently killed Ramagupta and married Dhruvadevi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements describe the traditional Ramagupta episode: the elder brother agreed to surrender Dhruvadevi, after which Chandragupta II killed the Saka king, killed Ramagupta and married Dhruvadevi.
accepted.tq: Test the succession dispute as a connected sequence of events.
accepted.sec: Ramagupta episode - source text, succession dispute  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological order:
A. First Huna attack during the reign of Kumaragupta I
B. Saka conquest by Chandragupta II
C. Later Huna waves during the reign of Skandagupta
D. Advance of Toramana into western and central India

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Saka conquest of Chandragupta II preceded the first Huna attack in late Kumaragupta I’s reign; later Huna waves occurred under Skandagupta, followed by Toramana’s advance under the weaker successors.
accepted.tq: Use the Gupta succession as the first framework, then place the invasions.
accepted.sec: Huna invasions → Huna leader + Gupta reign invaded + Indian ruler who repelled each (Toramana, Mihirakula)  [other exams]
